subject: Re: Switch economics — deferment credits and ops adaptor ask
message_1_body:
Hi Rachel + Monica,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Procurement asked for one consolidated ask from us: Bridgely needs (1) clarity on the credit/deferment structure you can offer if we commit to a 12‑month migration window, and (2) confirmation that the runtime surface (KV cache behavior + quantized builds) will be compatible with our existing on‑prem adapter — they flagged the adaptor work as the primary gating item.

Attached is a clean copy of the MA they expect to circulate internally (Bridgely_MA_proposal_v3.pdf). Can you send a short note outlining the credit schedule (timing + trigger events) and a high‑level compatibility matrix? Procurement would like a single PDF to attach to their CPO packet by EOD Thursday.

Appreciate it — Alexis

Attachment: Bridgely_MA_proposal_v3.pdf (application/pdf)
message_2_subject: Re: Switch economics — proposal and questions
message_2_body:
Hi Alexis —

Thanks for the clear ask and the MA. We can do both items; see summary below and I attached a one‑page matrix (runtime-compatibility-matrix.xlsx) and a short credit schedule you can drop into your packet. If procurement wants the legal language, we can draft the side letter once terms are agreed.

Quick answers: 
- Credit / deferment structure: We propose a two‑tier credit tied to signed SOW milestones: 15% consumption credit applied at contract start (month 0) and an additional 10% applied when the first production traffic is routed to Redwood (defined as sustained >500 requests/min for 3 consecutive days). Credits expire after 12 months. If Bridgely elects staged migration beyond 12 months, we can convert remaining credit to a one‑time onboarding rebate (non‑recurring).
- Commit and price anchoring: The credits require a 12‑month minimum commit on Dedicated capacity or hosted committed spend; we can offer a cap on unit price increases for the first 12 months.
- Runtime compatibility: Our runtime supports continuous KV caching and quantized runtimes; the adaptor work you described is usually a 2–4 week integration (sample adaptor shim we used for AcmeCorp took 3 weeks). I've attached a compatibility matrix and flagged the likely integration touchpoints. If you want, we can provide an engineer for a 2‑hour workshop next week to scope adaptor work.

Jordan / Karthik — can you confirm the SLA language we can share for the packet? Also tagging Monica for commercial approval of the 15%/10% split.

— Rachel

Attachment: runtime-compatibility-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
message_3_subject: Re: Switch economics — proposal and questions
message_3_body:
Rachel — this is exactly what procurement asked for, thank you. A couple quick follow ups from the CPO: 
1) Can the initial 15% credit be applied as a one‑time invoice credit (reduces first invoice) rather than spread across invoices? They prefer a single line item for oversight.
2) For the additional 10% post‑production, procurement wants the trigger definition codified (we'll include the >500 rps x 3 days language if you confirm).

Also — the CPO asked whether you can hold pricing for 45 days after signature (they need time to finalize an internal funding approval). If that hold is possible, we can circulate the MA with your summary and move to legal review Friday.

If possible, please include an engineer for the adaptor scoping workshop — procurement will treat that as a free technical due diligence session.

Thanks — Alexis

message_4_subject: Re: Switch economics — proposal and questions
message_4_body:
Thanks — quick internal note so we can be aligned before we send the packet to Bridgely: 

1) Invoice treatment: We agree to apply the 15% as a one‑time invoice credit on the first month’s invoice. Monica — please confirm that's within commercial guardrails (non‑recurring, reduces first invoice only).
2) Trigger language: Confirming the >500 req/min for 3 consecutive days as the production trigger for the 10% credit — we will include a monitoring clause that Redwood and Bridgely engineers must attest to in writing.
3) Price hold: We can hold proposed unit rates for 45 days post‑signature.
4) Workshop: Karthik will be the lead for the adaptor scoping workshop; he can do a 2‑hour session and produce a 1‑page integration plan and an estimate.

Monica — if commercial signs off, Rachel please send a single‑page credit schedule and the compatibility matrix to Alexis and procurement; we'll queue the side letter template for legal review in parallel.

— Jordan
